title: Information locality of a quantum locally recoverable code
summary: A classical linear code $C$ of length $n$ is said to have symbol locality $(r, δ)$ if for any index $j$ there exists a repair group $J_j \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n\}$ with $j\in J_j$ and $|J_j| \leq r+δ-1$ such that any $δ-1$ or fewer erasures in $J_j$ can be corrected by using codeword symbols only in $J_j$. Later it turned out that this way of defining $r$ overestimates the number of necessary codeword symbols for multiple-erasure correction, and information locality was proposed to define $r$ as the dimension of the punctured code of $C$ onto $J_j$.
